docs.text: HardFOC driver NTC Thermistor Driver ¶ A C++20 driver for NTC thermistors read through an ADC. It turns the voltage of a resistor divider into the thermistor's resistance and the resistance into degrees, with averaging, filtering and calibration, on any MCU with an ADC. Quickstart API guide Source on GitHub The driver has no platform code. You give it a small class that brings an ADC up and returns a channel's voltage; it does the rest: the divider equation, the Beta conversion, range checks, averaging, filtering and error codes. NTC chip thermistor, the driver's default part NTCG163JF103FT1S TDK Resistance 10 kΩ ± 1 % at 25 °C (R25) B constant 3435 K ± 1 % (B25/85) Operating range −40 °C to +150 °C Rated power 100 mW at 25 °C, still air Package 0603 (1.6 mm × 0.8 mm × 0.8 mm) Interface Analog: a resistor divider into any ADC input; the driver reads the node voltage Spec sheet What you get ¶ One object per sensor. NtcThermistor<YourAdc> takes a part type or a full ntc_config_t ; several sensors share one ADC. See API guide . Degrees from volts. The divider equation gives the resistance, the Beta equation the temperature, in °C, °F or K. See Conversion methods . Any NTC. Set R25, B and the series resistor for a 10 kΩ, 100 kΩ or other part; the TDK NTCG163JF103FT1S is the default. See Configuration . Clean readings. Multi-sample averaging, an exponential filter, a calibration offset and a valid range, with an NtcError for every failure. See API guide . Zero-overhead portability. The port is a CRTP class with seven small methods: no virtual calls in the ADC path, no heap, no RTOS dependency. See Porting . Tested without hardware. Host unit tests check the conversions against the TDK resistance table. See Testing and CI . Where to go next ¶ Quickstart Wire the divider, write the port, read a temperature in about 15 lines. API guide ¶ How to do the common jobs with the driver: configure, read, smooth, calibrate and handle errors. Every snippet on this page is compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/api_tasks.cpp , with Ntc standing for NtcThermistor<MyAdc> and MyAdc the port from Porting . The API reference lists every member. The shape of the API ¶ One NtcThermistor<AdcType> object per thermistor, holding an ntc_config_t and a pointer to your ADC port. Several objects can share one port, each on its own adc_channel . Group Calls Lifecycle Initialize() , Deinitialize() , IsInitialized() Read ReadTemperatureCelsius() , ReadTemperatureFahrenheit() , ReadTemperatureKelvin() , ReadTemperature() Raw values GetResistance() , GetVoltage() , GetRawAdcValue() Configure SetConfiguration() , GetConfiguration() , SetAdcChannel() , SetVoltageDivider() , SetReferenceVoltage() , SetBetaValue() , SetConversionMethod() Smooth SetSamplingParameters() , SetFiltering() Calibrate Calibrate() , SetCalibrationOffset() , GetCalibrationOffset() , ResetCalibration() Utilities CelsiusToFahrenheit() and the other unit conversions, GetErrorString() , GetTypeString() , GetDriverVersion() Initialize() returns bool ; every other call that can fail returns an NtcError and writes its result through a pointer. Nothing throws or allocates. Configure ¶ From a part type, then adjust the board-specific values: Ntc ntc ( NtcType :: NtcG163Jf103Ft1S , & adc ); // R25 = 10 kOhm, B = 3435 K, defaults for the rest if ( ntc . SetAdcChannel ( 2 ) != NtcError :: Success || ntc . SetVoltageDivider ( 10000.0F ) != NtcError :: Success || // series resistor (ohms) ntc . SetReferenceVoltage ( 3.3F ) != NtcError :: Success ) { // divider supply (V) return false ; } return ntc . Initialize (); Or from a full configuration, for any thermistor: ntc_config_t cfg = GetDefaultNtcConfig (); cfg . type = NtcType :: Custom ; cfg . resistance_at_25c = 100000.0F ; // a 100 kOhm part cfg . beta_value = 4250.0F ; // its B25/85 (or B25/50) from the datasheet cfg . series_resistance = 100000.0F ; // match R25 for the best resolution around 25 C cfg . reference_voltage = 3.3F ; cfg . adc_channel = 0 ; cfg . min_temperature = -20.0F ; // readings outside this window return TemperatureOutOfRange cfg . max_temperature = 100.0F ; Ntc ntc ( cfg , & adc ); return ntc . Initialize (); // false: invalid config, ADC not up, or no such channel Initialize() returns false when a value is invalid (R25, the supplies or the series resistor not positive; B outside 1000 K to 5000 K; sample_count zero; min_temperature not below max_temperature ; filter_alpha outside 0 to 1 with filtering on), when the port's EnsureInitialized() fails, or when IsChannelAvailable(adc_channel) is false. SetConfiguration() checks the same values and returns InvalidParameter . Configuration lists every field. Read ¶ ntc_reading_t r {}; if ( ntc . ReadTemperature ( & r ) == NtcError :: Success && r . is_valid ) { std :: printf ( "%.2f C %.2f F %.0f ohm %.3f V raw %lu 
 " , r . temperature_celsius , r . temperature_fahrenheit , r . resistance_ohms , r . voltage_volts , static_cast < unsigned long > ( r . adc_raw_value )); } float ohms = 0.0F ; if ( ntc . GetResistance ( & ohms ) == NtcError :: Success ) { std :: printf ( "thermistor: %.0f ohm 
 " , ohms ); } ReadTemperatureCelsius() is one conversion. ReadTemperature() fills every unit plus the resistance, voltage and raw count, but reads the ADC again for each of those: with averaging on, it costs four times the samples. timestamp_us is always 0 and accuracy_celsius always 0.5; fill in your own if you need them. Smooth ¶ ntc . SetSamplingParameters ( 16 , 0 ); // average 16 ADC reads per reading ntc . SetFiltering ( true , 0.2F ); // then an EMA: new = 0.2 * reading + 0.8 * previous Setting Effect Cost sample_count Averages that many ADC reads; failed reads are skipped sample_count reads per call sample_delay_ms A busy-wait loop between samples, not a timed delay CPU time, length depends on the MCU enable_filtering , filter_alpha EMA after calibration: new = α · reading + (1 − α) · previous None; the first reading seeds it Prefer sample_delay_ms = 0 and space your calls with your RTOS. A smaller α smooths more and responds more slowly; changing the filter or the configuration resets it. Calibrate ¶ // With the sensor at a known temperature (a reference thermometer reads 23.4 C): ntc . ResetCalibration (); if ( ntc . Calibrate ( 23.4F ) == NtcError :: Success ) { float offset = 0.0F ; ntc . GetCalibrationOffset ( & offset ); // store it; restore with SetCalibrationOffset(offset) std :: printf ( "offset %.2f C 
 " , offset ); } Calibrate(t) reads the sensor and sets the offset to t − reading . The reading already includes the current offset, so call ResetCalibration() first, as above. The offset is a constant: it corrects R25 tolerance and divider errors well, and the Beta equation's error only near the calibration temperature ( Conversion methods ). The offset lives in RAM; store it yourself. Handle errors ¶ float c = 0.0F ; switch ( const NtcError err = ntc . ReadTemperatureCelsius ( & c ); err ) { case NtcError :: Success : break ; case NtcError :: ConversionFailed : // node at 0 V or at the supply: shorted or open sensor case NtcError :: TemperatureOutOfRange : // converted, but outside min/max_temperature std :: printf ( "sensor fault: %s 
 " , Ntc :: GetErrorString ( err )); break ; default : // AdcReadFailed, Timeout, HardwareFault, NotInitialized ... std :: printf ( "ADC: %s 
 " , Ntc :: GetErrorString ( err )); break ; } NtcError Meaning Where to look NotInitialized Initialize() not called or failed Your port's EnsureInitialized() NullPointer A null output pointer, or no ADC port The call site AdcReadFailed , Timeout , HardwareFault Your port returned ReadFailed , Timeout or HardwareError Your port InvalidParameter A setter or SetConfiguration() rejected a value; or InvalidChannel from the port The value ConversionFailed The node at 0 V or at V_REF, or a resistance outside 0.1 Ω to 1 MΩ Wiring: shorted or open sensor TemperatureOutOfRange Converted, but outside min_temperature to max_temperature The range, or a real over-temperature With averaging on, a single failed sample is skipped; the call fails with AdcReadFailed only when every sample fails. GetErrorString() returns a short text for each code. Next ¶ Configuration lists every field; Troubleshooting maps symptoms to causes.

docs.text: Architecture ¶ How the driver is put together: three layers, what each owns, and how one reading reaches the ADC. Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application talks to one NtcThermistor object, whose public calls (listed from inc/ntc_thermistor.hpp) read the temperature, the resistance and the voltage, and set the divider, the sampling, the filter and the calibration. The core turns a node voltage into the thermistor's resistance and the resistance into a temperature with the Beta equation or a lookup table (inc/ntc_conversion.hpp). The ADC interface (AdcInterface in inc/ntc_adc_interface.hpp) is a CRTP base that forwards to your class. The platform port is the only code you write: a class that brings the ADC up and returns a channel's voltage and count. Below it is the hardware: the divider and the thermistor. Drawn from: inc/ntc_thermistor.hpp NtcThermistor public calls ; inc/ntc_adc_interface.hpp AdcInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . The three layers ¶ Layer Where You change it when Core : NtcThermistor<AdcType> , conversions inc/ntc_thermistor.hpp , src/ Never, for a new board ADC interface : ntc::AdcInterface<Derived> inc/ntc_adc_interface.hpp Never Platform port : your class Your project Once per MCU or board ( Porting ) The core depends only on the port's methods; the port depends only on your SDK. Everything above the port is the same on ESP32, STM32, a Linux host or the unit-test model. That is how the host tests run the real driver code without hardware. How one reading reaches the ADC ¶ sequenceDiagram participant A as Application participant D as NtcThermistor participant C as NTC:: conversions participant P as Your port A->>D: ReadTemperatureCelsius(&c) loop sample_count times D->>P: ReadChannelV(adc_channel, &v) P-->>D: AdcError::Success, volts end D->>C: CalculateThermistorResistance(v, V_REF, R_SERIES) C-->>D: ohms D->>C: ConvertResistanceToTemperatureBeta(ohms, R25, B) C-->>D: degrees C D->>D: + offset, EMA filter, min/max check D-->>A: NtcError::Success, c Why CRTP ¶ ntc::AdcInterface takes your class as a template parameter instead of declaring virtual functions. The compiler sees your port's methods directly and inlines them: the ADC path has no vtable, allocates nothing and needs no RTTI. The driver type names the port, NtcThermistor<MyAdc> . NtcThermistor only calls the methods by name, so any class with the same seven methods works; deriving from ntc::AdcInterface documents the contract and keeps the port from being copied. NtcThermistor itself has a virtual destructor, so each driver object carries one vtable pointer. docs.text: Configuration ¶ Every field of ntc_config_t , its default and the setter that changes it at run time. GetDefaultNtcConfig() returns the defaults below (the NTCG163JF103FT1S on channel 0 of a 3.3 V, 10 kΩ divider). The constructor that takes an NtcType starts from the same defaults and loads that type's R25 and B. Change any field before construction, or with SetConfiguration() afterwards. Fields ¶ Field Default Setter type NtcG163Jft103Ft1S constructor resistance_at_25c (Ω) 10000 SetConfiguration() beta_value (K) 3435 SetBetaValue() reference_voltage (V) 3.3 SetReferenceVoltage() series_resistance (Ω) 10000 SetVoltageDivider() calibration_offset (°C) 0 SetCalibrationOffset() , Calibrate() conversion_method Auto SetConversionMethod() adc_channel 0 SetAdcChannel() adc_resolution_bits 12 not used in the conversion sample_count 1 SetSamplingParameters() sample_delay_ms 0 SetSamplingParameters() min_temperature (°C) −40 SetConfiguration() max_temperature (°C) 125 SetConfiguration() enable_filtering false SetFiltering() filter_alpha 0.1 SetFiltering() What each one means ¶ resistance_at_25c , beta_value The thermistor's R25 and B from its datasheet. docs.text: Conversion methods ¶ How the driver turns a voltage into a temperature, which equation each method uses and how accurate each is for the NTCG163JF103FT1S. The pipeline ¶ flowchart LR A["ADC: V_NODE"] --> B["Divider: R = R_SERIES · V / (V_REF − V)"] B --> C["Beta: 1/T = 1/T25 + ln(R/R25) / B"] C --> D["+ calibration_offset"] D --> E["EMA filter (optional)"] E --> F["min/max check"] Every reading follows these steps in ReadTemperatureCelsius() : average sample_count voltages, solve the divider, convert, add the calibration offset, filter, and check the result against min_temperature and max_temperature . Beta equation (what the driver uses) ¶ 1/T = 1/T25 + ln(R / R25) / B T and T25 in kelvin, T25 = 298.15 K NTC::ConvertResistanceToTemperatureBeta() implements it, and the driver calls it for NtcConversionMethod::Mathematical , for Auto (the default) and whenever the lookup table does not cover a reading. B is a two-point fit: the datasheet's B25/85 makes the equation exact at 25 °C and 85 °C and leaves an error elsewhere. For the NTCG163JF103FT1S (R25 = 10 kΩ, B25/85 = 3435 K), against the spec sheet's nominal resistance: Temperature (°C) Beta reads (°C) Error (°C) −40 −35.56 +4.44 −20 −17.47 +2.53 0 1.11 +1.11 25 25.00 0.00 50 49.58 −0.42 85 85.01 +0.01 100 100.50 +0.50 125 126.68 +1.68 150 153.19 +3.19 Derived from Table 3 of the spec sheet ; the host tests check the 0 °C, 25 °C, 85 °C, 125 °C and −40 °C rows. Between 10 °C and 95 °C the error stays under 0.6 °C. Outside it, use the Steinhart-Hart equation below, or a calibration offset near the temperature that matters to you. Using B25/50 instead (3382 K on TDK's product page for the NTCG163JF103FT1) moves the exact points to 25 °C and 50 °C and shifts the error to higher temperatures. Use the B your datasheet gives for the range you care about. Steinhart-Hart equation ¶ 1/T = A + B · ln(R) + C · ln(R)³ Three coefficients fitted at three temperatures follow the curve far better than Beta. Fitted to the spec sheet at −40 °C, 25 °C and 125 °C, the coefficients below stay within 0.2 °C of the nominal table from −40 °C to +125 °C and within 0.41 °C at +150 °C ( derived ): // Coefficients fitted to the NTCG163JF103FT1S table at -40, 25 and 125 C. constexpr float A = 0.8767633e-3F ; constexpr float B = 2.527899e-4F ; constexpr float C = 1.906681e-7F ; float ohms = 0.0F ; if ( ntc . GetResistance ( & ohms ) != NtcError :: Success || ohms <= 0.0F ) { return false ; } const float ln_r = std :: log ( ohms ); celsius = 1.0F / ( A + B * ln_r + C * ln_r * ln_r * ln_r ) - 273.15F ; return true ; The driver does not call Steinhart-Hart itself. Read the resistance with GetResistance() and apply the equation, as above. Library Steinhart-Hart helpers NTC::ConvertResistanceToTemperatureSteinhartHart() rejects any C coefficient above 1 × 10⁻⁷, which excludes the fit for this part (C ≈ 1.9 × 10⁻⁷); NTC::CalculateSteinhartHartCoefficients() does not return a usable fit; and NTC::ConvertResistanceToTemperatureDefault() uses generic coefficients that read about 9 °C low at 85 °C for this part. Evaluate the equation yourself until these are fixed. Lookup table ¶ NtcConversionMethod::LookupTable searches a per-type table and interpolates. The table shipped in src/ntc_lookup_table.cpp does not match the NTCG163JF103FT1S datasheet: it spans 336.7 Ω down to negative values, so a reading above 336.7 Ω (every temperature below about 145 °C) falls outside it and the driver falls back to the Beta equation. Below 336.7 Ω the table's interpolation returns values that are wrong. Use Auto or Mathematical until the table is regenerated from the spec sheet. docs.text: Hardware ¶ How to build the divider the driver expects, how to size it for your temperature range, and what limits the accuracy. Part values here come from the TDK NTCG163JF103FT1S spec sheet , the driver's default part. Values marked derived are computed from that sheet's nominal resistance table for a 3.3 V, 10 kΩ / 10 kΩ divider and a 12-bit ADC; recompute them for your values. Divider ¶ reference_voltage (V) V_REF, the divider supply that feeds R_SERIES series_resistance (Ω) R_SERIES, from V_REF to the ADC node resistance_at_25c , beta_value The NTC, from the ADC node to GND adc_channel The ADC input on the node The driver solves the divider for the thermistor: R NTC = R SERIES · V NODE / (V REF − V NODE ) It assumes this orientation, the NTC on the low side. The voltage falls as the temperature rises. A board with the NTC on the high side With the thermistor from the supply to the node and the resistor to ground, the equation above returns R SERIES ² / R NTC . Return V REF − V NODE from your port's ReadChannelV() instead of V NODE , and the driver sees the low-side divider it expects. Supply and reference ¶ The driver uses the node voltage in volts and reference_voltage as the divider's supply. Two consequences: Set reference_voltage to the voltage that feeds R_SERIES , measured on your board, not the ADC's nominal full scale. A 1 % error in it moves the reading by about 0.5 °C at 25 °C ( derived ). Supply noise goes straight into the reading. Feed the divider from the same clean rail as the ADC reference, or from a reference output if your MCU has one. adc_resolution_bits in the configuration and GetReferenceVoltage() / GetResolutionBits() in the port are not used in the conversion; the volts your port returns are. Choosing the series resistor ¶ Resolution is best where R NTC equals R SERIES . For a 10 kΩ part, 10 kΩ centres the divider on 25 °C: Temperature (°C) V NODE (V) °C per LSB −35 3.086 0.08 0 2.415 0.03 25 1.650 0.03 85 0.418 0.08 125 0.167 0.22 Derived from the spec sheet's Table 3 for 3.3 V, 10 kΩ and a 12-bit ADC (0.81 mV per LSB); the slope is −30.8 mV/°C at 25 °C and −3.6 mV/°C at 125 °C. For a range that sits away from 25 °C, choose R SERIES near R NTC at its centre; NTC::CalculateOptimalSeriesResistance() returns the geometric mean of R NTC at the two ends of a range (it assumes B = 3435 K). Use a 1 % or better resistor with a low temperature coefficient, and keep it away from the heat you measure. ADC input and filtering ¶ The ADC sees the divider's source resistance, R SERIES ∥ R NTC : 5 kΩ at 25 °C for 10 kΩ / 10 kΩ. If your ADC's sample-and-hold needs a lower source resistance, or the wire to the sensor is long, add C_FILT from the node to ground (10 nF to 100 nF is common). The node then settles with a time constant of source resistance × C_FILT, 0.5 ms for 5 kΩ and 100 nF: wait several time constants after powering the divider before sampling. Averaging in the driver ( sample_count ) reduces random ADC noise; it does not remove an offset or a gain error. Use your MCU's ADC calibration for those (on ESP32, the adc_cali driver). Self-heating ¶ The current through the divider heats the thermistor. The power in the NTC is largest when R NTC = R SERIES : V REF ² / (4 · R SERIES ), 272 µW for 3.3 V and 10 kΩ ( derived ). The temperature rise is that power divided by the dissipation constant of the mounted part, which depends on the board; the TDK spec sheet in this repository does not state one. With 1 mW/°C it would be 0.27 °C. To reduce it: use a larger R25 and R SERIES (100 kΩ parts dissipate a tenth as much), or power the divider from a GPIO only while you sample. Part limits ¶ Parameter NTCG163JF103FT1S R25 10 kΩ ± 1 % B25/85 3435 K ± 1 % Operating temperature −40 °C to +150 °C Maximum rated power 100 mW at 25 °C, still air Size 1.6 mm × 0.8 mm × 0.8 mm (0603) A 1 % R25 tolerance alone is about ±0.26 °C at 25 °C ( derived : 1 % ÷ (B / T²)). The spec sheet's Table 3 gives the minimum, nominal and maximum resistance from −40 °C to +150 °C in 5 °C steps; the driver's host tests check its conversions against the nominal column. The driver's default window is −40 °C to +125 °C ( min_temperature , max_temperature ). Widen it to use the part up to +150 °C. Supported part types ¶ NtcType Part NtcG163Jf103Ft1S TDK NTCG163JF103FT1S, spec sheet in docs/datasheet/ NtcG163Jft103Ft1S Not found in TDK's listings; same values NtcG164Jf103Ft1S Not in TDK's listings; same values Custom Any NTC: set R25 and B ( Configuration ) All three TDK types load R25 = 10 kΩ and B = 3435 K. For any other thermistor, use Custom with the values from its datasheet. docs.text: Installation ¶ Add the driver to a CMake or ESP-IDF project. It is a small C++20 library: two source files and a header-only template, with no dependencies. Requirements ¶ A C++20 compiler (the headers use designated initialisers): GCC 10+, Clang 12+ or a current MSVC. The C++ standard library's <cmath> . No RTOS, heap or exceptions: every driver call is noexcept and returns bool or an NtcError . Get the source ¶ A git submodule keeps the driver pinned to a version you chose: git submodule add https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-ntc-thermistor-driver.git external/hf-ntc-thermistor-driver git submodule update --init external/hf-ntc-thermistor-driver Only inc/ , src/ , cmake/ and CMakeLists.txt are needed to build. The examples have their own submodule ( examples/esp32/scripts ); you do not need it to use the driver. CMake ¶ add_subdirectory ( external/hf-ntc-thermistor-driver ) target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE hf_ntc_thermistor ) The hf_ntc_thermistor target is a static library ( src/ntc_conversion.cpp , src/ntc_lookup_table.cpp ). It carries the include directories and requires C++20 ( cxx_std_20 ), so your target does not need to set either. Option Default Effect HF_NTC_THERMISTOR_ENABLE_WARNINGS OFF -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic on the driver sources HF_NTC_THERMISTOR_BUILD_TESTS OFF Builds the host unit tests in tests/ ( Testing and CI ) ESP-IDF ¶ The ESP-IDF component wrapper is examples/esp32/components/hf_ntc_thermistor/ . Copy that folder into your project's components/ (or point EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS at it) and set the HF_NTC_THERMISTOR_ROOT cache variable to the driver checkout; the wrapper stops with a clear message when the path is wrong. Your component then declares REQUIRES hf_ntc_thermistor . How the build is organised ¶ Layer File Role Settings cmake/hf_ntc_thermistor_build_settings.cmake Sources, include directories, version: the single source of truth Library CMakeLists.txt Static library for host builds and CI ESP-IDF examples/esp32/components/hf_ntc_thermistor/CMakeLists.txt IDF component wrapper over the same settings The version is set once in the settings file and written into ntc_thermistor_version.h at configure time. Read it at run time: const char * v = GetNtcThermistorDriverVersion (); // "1.0.0" The root CMakeLists.txt writes a package configuration but has no install() rules yet: use the driver with add_subdirectory() or the ESP-IDF component, not find_package() . Next ¶ Quickstart wires a divider and reads a temperature; Porting writes the ADC interface for your MCU.

docs.text: Porting ¶ Run the driver on a new MCU by writing one class: the ADC interface. The driver never calls your SDK directly. It calls seven methods on a class you derive from ntc::AdcInterface<Self> (in inc/ntc_adc_interface.hpp ). The base class uses CRTP: the calls are resolved at compile time, so there are no virtual functions, no vtable and nothing to allocate. Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application talks to one NtcThermistor object, whose public calls (listed from inc/ntc_thermistor.hpp) read the temperature, the resistance and the voltage, and set the divider, the sampling, the filter and the calibration. The core turns a node voltage into the thermistor's resistance and the resistance into a temperature with the Beta equation or a lookup table (inc/ntc_conversion.hpp). The ADC interface (AdcInterface in inc/ntc_adc_interface.hpp) is a CRTP base that forwards to your class. The platform port is the only code you write: a class that brings the ADC up and returns a channel's voltage and count. Below it is the hardware: the divider and the thermistor. Drawn from: inc/ntc_thermistor.hpp NtcThermistor public calls ; inc/ntc_adc_interface.hpp AdcInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . What you implement ¶ Method Contract IsInitialized() const true once the ADC is ready EnsureInitialized() Bring the ADC up if needed; true on success. Called by Initialize() IsChannelAvailable(channel) const true for a channel this port can read ReadChannelV(channel, &volts) One conversion, as the voltage at the pin in volts. Used for every temperature ReadChannelCount(channel, &count) One conversion, as the raw count. Used only by GetRawAdcValue() GetReferenceVoltage() const The ADC's full-scale voltage. Not used by the driver today GetResolutionBits() const The ADC's resolution. Not used by the driver today The read methods return ntc::AdcError : Success , or NotInitialized , InvalidChannel , ReadFailed , Timeout , HardwareError . The driver maps them to NtcError ( API guide ). The port ¶ my_adc.hpp class MyAdc : public ntc :: AdcInterface < MyAdc > { public : static constexpr uint8_t kChannels = 7 ; // ADC1 channels 0..6 on this MCU static constexpr uint8_t kBits = 12 ; static constexpr float kFullScaleV = 3.3F ; // input range at the chosen attenuation [[ nodiscard ]] bool IsInitialized () const { return ready_ ; } // Bring the ADC up once; later calls return true at once. bool EnsureInitialized () { if ( ! ready_ ) { ready_ = platform_adc_init (); } return ready_ ; } [[ nodiscard ]] bool IsChannelAvailable ( uint8_t channel ) const { return channel < kChannels ; } ntc :: AdcError ReadChannelCount ( uint8_t channel , uint32_t * count ) { uint32_t mv = 0 ; return read ( channel , count , & mv ); } // The driver reads volts: return the calibrated voltage at the pin, not count * Vref / 4095. ntc :: AdcError ReadChannelV ( uint8_t channel , float * voltage_v ) { uint32_t raw = 0 ; uint32_t mv = 0 ; const ntc :: AdcError err = read ( channel , & raw , & mv ); if ( err == ntc :: AdcError :: Success ) { * voltage_v = static_cast < float > ( mv ) / 1000.0F ; } return err ; } [[ nodiscard ]] float GetReferenceVoltage () const { return kFullScaleV ; } [[ nodiscard ]] uint8_t GetResolutionBits () const { return kBits ; } private : ntc :: AdcError read ( uint8_t channel , uint32_t * raw , uint32_t * mv ) { if ( ! ready_ ) { return ntc :: AdcError :: NotInitialized ; } if ( ! IsChannelAvailable ( channel )) { return ntc :: AdcError :: InvalidChannel ; } if ( ! platform_adc_read ( channel , * raw , * mv )) { return ntc :: AdcError :: ReadFailed ; } return ntc :: AdcError :: Success ; } bool ready_ = false ; }; Rules for ReadChannelV() : Return calibrated volts. The driver's accuracy is the accuracy of this number. Use your SDK's ADC calibration (on ESP32, adc_cali_raw_to_voltage() ), not count × V_full / 4095 . One conversion per call. The driver averages sample_count calls itself. Block until the result is ready , or return Timeout . Use an input range that covers the node. With a 3.3 V divider the node spans about 0.1 V to 3.1 V over −40 °C to +150 °C; pick the attenuation or gain that covers it. Reference implementation ¶ The ESP32 example's port, mock_esp32_adc.hpp , is a simulated ADC: it returns a fixed mid-scale count and does not touch the hardware. It shows the shape of a port, not an ESP-IDF ADC driver. On ESP-IDF, implement EnsureInitialized() with adc_oneshot_new_unit() , adc_oneshot_config_channel() and an adc_cali scheme, and ReadChannelV() with adc_oneshot_read() and adc_cali_raw_to_voltage() . Check your port ¶ Build it: the port on this page is compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/my_adc.hpp , with the driver instantiated over it. Replace the thermistor with a 10 kΩ 0.1 % resistor: GetVoltage() returns half the supply and ReadTemperatureCelsius() returns 25 °C within a few tenths of a degree, set by the two resistors and the ADC calibration. Short the node to ground: ConversionFailed . Open the thermistor: ConversionFailed , or TemperatureOutOfRange if ADC noise keeps the node just under the supply. Threads ¶ The driver is not thread-safe. Give each NtcThermistor one owner task, or guard every call on a driver object (and its ADC port) with one mutex. Several thermistors on one port need that mutex around the port too.

Wire it ¶ The thermistor sits between the ADC node and ground; the series resistor between the supply and the node. From To Notes 3.3 V R_SERIES 10 kΩ, 1 % or better; the supply value goes in reference_voltage R_SERIES ADC input The divider node ADC input NTC NTCG163JF103FT1S or any 10 kΩ NTC NTC GND Same ground as the ADC Keep the node voltage inside the ADC's input range. With 3.3 V and 10 kΩ / 10 kΩ it is 1.65 V at 25 °C and moves toward 0 V as the sensor heats. The Hardware page covers resistor choice, filtering and self-heating. 2. Add the driver ¶ Add the repository as a submodule and link the hf_ntc_thermistor CMake target. Installation covers CMake and ESP-IDF. git submodule add https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-ntc-thermistor-driver.git external/hf-ntc-thermistor-driver 3. Write the port ¶ The port is the only platform code. It brings the ADC up and returns a channel's voltage and raw count. IsChannelAvailable ( channel )) { return ntc :: AdcError :: InvalidChannel ; } if ( ! platform_adc_read ( channel , * raw , * mv )) { return ntc :: AdcError :: ReadFailed ; } return ntc :: AdcError :: Success ; } bool ready_ = false ; }; Return the calibrated voltage at the pin from ReadChannelV() : the driver computes the resistance from it. Porting explains each method. 4. Read the temperature ¶ main.cpp #include "ntc_thermistor.hpp" #include <cstdio> int read_board_temperature ( MyAdc & adc , float & celsius ) { ntc_config_t cfg = GetDefaultNtcConfig (); // NTCG163JF103FT1S: 10 kOhm at 25 C, B 3435 K cfg . adc_channel = 2 ; // 1. the ADC input on the divider node cfg . series_resistance = 10000.0F ; // 2. the resistor from the supply to the node cfg . reference_voltage = 3.3F ; // 3. the supply of the divider NtcThermistor < MyAdc > ntc ( cfg , & adc ); if ( ! ntc . Initialize ()) { // 4. ADC up, channel present, config valid return -1 ; } const NtcError err = ntc . ReadTemperatureCelsius ( & celsius ); // 5. volts -> ohms -> C if ( err != NtcError :: Success ) { std :: printf ( "NTC: %s \n " , NtcThermistor < MyAdc >:: GetErrorString ( err )); return -2 ; } return 0 ; } What each step does: adc_channel selects the input your port reads. series_resistance is the resistor between the supply and the node, in ohms. reference_voltage is the divider's supply voltage. The driver solves R NTC = R SERIES · V / (V REF − V) with it. Initialize() checks the configuration, brings the ADC up and checks the channel. ReadTemperatureCelsius() reads the voltage, converts it and checks the result against min_temperature / max_temperature (−40 °C to +125 °C by default). This example is built by the host CI, so it compiles against the current headers. docs.text: Testing and CI ¶ How the driver is checked: host unit tests against a model of the divider, compiled documentation, an ESP32 build and static analysis, on every pull request. Host unit tests ¶ The tests build the real driver against a model of an ADC reading the divider node. A test sets the thermistor's resistance; the model returns the node voltage and count. Readings are checked against the nominal resistance table of the TDK NTCG163JF103FT1S (25 °C, 85 °C, 0 °C, 125 °C and −40 °C), and ADC failures are injected. cmake -S . -B build-host -DHF_NTC_THERMISTOR_BUILD_TESTS = ON cmake --build build-host ctest --test-dir build-host --output-on-failure File Covers tests/test_driver.cpp Initialisation, Beta accuracy against the table, errors, averaging, open and short, range, calibration, filter, free functions tests/mock_adc.hpp The ADC and divider model tests/test_harness.hpp A small test registry and check macros Documentation snippets ¶ Every C++ block on this site is included from tests/docs/ , which the host build compiles (target hf_ntc_thermistor_doc_snippets ) with the driver instantiated over the documented port. A change to the API that breaks a page breaks the build first. CI workflows ¶ Workflow What it checks Host unit tests GCC and Clang build and run the tests and the doc snippets ESP32 examples build Every app in examples/esp32/app_config.yml , for each listed ESP-IDF version and build type C++ lint, C++ analysis clang-format, clang-tidy and cppcheck Docs Strict site build, figure and generated-table drift, Doxygen, link check, Lighthouse budget Markdown lint, YAML lint, link check Repository text files The workflows call the shared, versioned workflows of hf-general-ci-tools and hf-espidf-ci-tools . On hardware ¶ The ESP32 example runs over a simulated ADC. To check a real board, follow Porting : a precision resistor in place of the thermistor gives a known 25 °C.

docs.text: The tests build the real driver against a model of an ADC reading the divider node. A test sets the thermistor's resistance; the model returns the node voltage and count. Readings are checked against the nominal resistance table of the TDK NTCG163JF103FT1S (25 °C, 85 °C, 0 °C, 125 °C and −40 °C), and ADC failures are injected. cmake -S . -B build-host -DHF_NTC_THERMISTOR_BUILD_TESTS = ON cmake --build build-host ctest --test-dir build-host --output-on-failure File Covers tests/test_driver.cpp Initialisation, Beta accuracy against the table, errors, averaging, open and short, range, calibration, filter, free functions tests/mock_adc.hpp The ADC and divider model tests/test_harness.hpp A small test registry and check macros

docs.text: Troubleshooting ¶ Symptoms you may see while bringing up an NTC thermistor, their causes and the fix for each. Start with the voltage: GetVoltage() and GetResistance() on a failing reading tell wiring and ADC problems (the voltage is wrong) apart from configuration problems (the resistance is right, the degrees are not). Initialize() returns false ¶ Cause Check Fix ADC not up Your port's EnsureInitialized() Fix the SDK call Channel missing IsChannelAvailable(adc_channel) in your port Use a channel the port accepts Invalid config R25, supply or series resistor not positive; B outside 1000 K to 5000 K; min_temperature ≥ max_temperature ; sample_count 0 Correct the value; SetConfiguration() returns InvalidParameter for the same cases No port nullptr passed to the constructor Pass the port's address Temperature conversion failed ¶ The node reads 0 V or the supply, or the resistance is outside 0.1 Ω to 1 MΩ. Cause Check Fix Thermistor shorted or missing to the node GetVoltage() near 0 V Wiring, solder joints Thermistor open GetVoltage() near the supply Wiring, connector, cable Port returns counts, not volts GetVoltage() returns thousands Return volts from ReadChannelV() ( Porting ) reference_voltage below the real supply GetVoltage() above reference_voltage Set the divider's real supply Temperature out of range ¶ The conversion worked but the result is outside min_temperature to max_temperature (−40 °C to +125 °C by default). Read GetResistance() : if it matches the thermistor's table at the real temperature, widen the window; if not, see the next section. A part near a hot spot may be right. Off by a few degrees ¶ Cause Check Fix Wrong supply value Measure the divider supply Set reference_voltage to it: 1 % is about 0.5 °C at 25 °C Wrong series resistor Measure it Set series_resistance Uncalibrated ADC GetVoltage() against a meter Use your SDK's ADC calibration in ReadChannelV() Beta error far from 25 °C to 85 °C The error grows with distance: +4.4 °C at −40 °C for this part Steinhart-Hart or a calibration offset ( Conversion methods ) Wrong B for the part B25/50 and B25/85 differ by 1 % to 2 % Use the B for your range Self-heating Reading drops when you lower the divider current Larger resistors, or power the divider only while sampling ( Hardware ) LookupTable method The setting in conversion_method Use Auto ( Conversion methods ) Reading moves the wrong way ¶ The temperature falls as the part heats: the thermistor is on the high side of the divider. Swap the two parts, or return V REF − V NODE from the port ( Hardware ). Noisy readings ¶ Cause Fix ADC noise SetSamplingParameters(16, 0) Slow drift or ripple SetFiltering(true, 0.1F) ; a smaller α smooths more Long wire to the sensor, high source resistance C_FILT, 10 nF to 100 nF from the node to ground Supply ripple Feed the divider from a clean rail ( Hardware ) Calibration made it worse ¶ Calibrate() measures with the current offset applied and replaces it. Call ResetCalibration() before Calibrate() , and calibrate at the temperature you care about most.

docs.text: Figures ¶ Every figure on this site is drawn by a Python module from facts extracted from the code, so it is rebuilt, not redrawn, when the code changes. CI runs hardfoc-docs figures --check and fails when a committed figure no longer matches the code. Each figure below lists the files it is drawn from. Three layers, one of them yours ¶ Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application talks to one NtcThermistor object, whose public calls (listed from inc/ntc_thermistor.hpp) read the temperature, the resistance and the voltage, and set the divider, the sampling, the filter and the calibration. The core turns a node voltage into the thermistor's resistance and the resistance into a temperature with the Beta equation or a lookup table (inc/ntc_conversion.hpp). The ADC interface (AdcInterface in inc/ntc_adc_interface.hpp) is a CRTP base that forwards to your class. The platform port is the only code you write: a class that brings the ADC up and returns a channel's voltage and count. Below it is the hardware: the divider and the thermistor.
